references.note: Theorem 4(1), p. 9: if x_n exceeds its tail X_n for every n, the subsum set is the disjoint union of 2^n closed intervals at each level n, a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure lim 2^k X_k (credited to H. Hornich, 1941).
references.title: Z. Nitecki, Subsum sets: intervals, Cantor sets, and Cantorvals, arXiv:1106.3779v2 (2013), Theorem 4

references.note: Each term 1/(2^n − 1) exceeds the sum of all later terms, which is Nitecki's hypothesis; the paper itself claims only a topological Cantor set.

literature_proposed.summary: Elementary from Nitecki's Theorem 4(1) (Hornich 1941): the measure is lim 2^k X_k with X_k = Σ_{j>k} 1/(2^j − 1), and 2^k X_k = Σ_{j≥1} 1/(2^j − 2^(−k)) decreases to Σ 2^(−j) = 1. This is the precise content of Kovač's remark (erdosproblems.com/257 forum) that the subsum set is a 'fat' Cantor set.

justification.text: Real division; the divisor is zero only at n = 0, where the term is Lean's junk value 0, so A and A \ {0} give the same sum and the set of sums is unchanged; the informal statement never uses n = 0.

review.words: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is $$ \sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} $$ irrational?

statement.text:
import Mathlib
import Nodes.«variant-f9c7b81b».Context

/-- The set of subset sums of the Mersenne reciprocals, `{Σ_{n∈A} 1/(2^n-1) : A ⊆ ℕ}`, has
Lebesgue measure exactly `1` (the term at `n = 0` is Lean's junk value `0`, so `A` and `A \ {0}`
give the same sum). It is a Cantor set (Kovač–Tao, arXiv:2406.17593, Rem. 4.1: distinct `A` give
distinct sums) of positive measure inside `[0, 1.6067…]`: about 62% of the interval. Erdős 257
asks whether it meets ℚ only in the sums of finite sets; its positive measure is why Kovač
(erdosproblems.com/257) expects the answer to be no. Proof: the sums of sets with prescribed
elements below `N` fill `2^(N-1)` disjoint intervals of length `T_N = Σ_{k≥N} 1/(2^k-1)`
(disjoint by the gap lemma), and `2^(N-1) T_N → 1`. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_subsum_set_volume :
    MeasureTheory.volume {x : ℝ | ∃ A : Set ℕ, ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1) = x} = 1 := by
  sorry
